# Tiny Little Office links

Tiny Little Office (https://tinylittleoffice.com) is an office suite whose documents live entirely in their links. You make a document by writing a URL. Nothing is uploaded or stored: opening the link shows the document in an editor, whoever opens it can change it, and the address changes with every edit, so the new link is the new document. Nothing is sent to a server: the document sits after the `#`, which browsers never send.

Every document is one text in one format, TLO: Markdown with a few additions. If you can write Markdown you can write any app below; each section says which shapes that app reads, with one of its own templates as the example.

<!-- This file is written by scripts/make-skill.ts from SKILL.tpl.md: edit the template, then `npm run skill`. -->

## The URL

```
https://tinylittleoffice.com/<app>/#title=<title>&doc=<document>
```

- `<app>` is one of the apps below (the table's first column).
- `doc` is the document, URL-encoded: a new line is `%0A`, a space `+` or `%20`; `& # % + =` in the text must be percent-encoded. Non-ASCII is fine, percent-encoded as UTF-8.
- `title` (optional) is the document's name. `by` (optional) is who made it: your name as an agent, say. It is a claim, in your own word (below).
- `view` (optional) opens the document another way: `pdf`, `png`, `html`, `md` or `tlo` download it as it opens, as do an app's own formats (listed under each app); `embed` is the pages alone, for a frame; on a deck, `show` opens it presenting.
- `md=` may stand for `doc=`: it is the same text (TLO is Markdown). With no app in the path or the head, `md=` opens a text in the Word Processor.
- The document's own head may name the app instead: a `doc` that begins `---%0Aapp: sheet%0A---` needs no app in the path (`https://tinylittleoffice.com/#doc=...`).

Put the parameters after `#`, exactly as shown, never after `?`. On opening, the link is rewritten into its packed form, `#/v1/<app>/<payload>`, which is what the person shares onward. Give them the link you wrote; they need not know its format.

Length: a QR code holds at most 2,953 characters and some chat apps cut a link past about 2,000. Keep the whole URL under 2,000 where you can; a short link (below) holds more.

The packed form: after `#/v1/<app>/` comes one letter and then base64url bytes (with `~` for 62 where RFC 4648 has `-`, so a pasted link never breaks at a hyphen; `-` is read too): the document's TLO text deflated against a dictionary of TLO's own words (`y`), deflated (`z`), or raw (`r`). `?d` after it opens the pages to read rather than the editor; `?show` opens a deck presenting; `#/v1/<app>.<ext>/…` downloads the file as it opens. You never need to make these by hand: the plain form becomes the shortest of them when opened, and the API below makes them directly.

## Sharing: a link is a copy

There is no shared document. Whoever opens a link gets their own copy: what they change is in their link, not in the one they were sent, and nobody else sees it unless they send their new link back. Never promise collaboration, live editing or one copy that everyone fills in. For a sign-up sheet, a form to fill in or work to hand in, tell the person that each one who opens it makes their own copy and should send their link back. A short link (below) can be updated by its owner, so later visitors get the owner's new version; it never gathers anyone else's changes.

## TLO: Markdown, and what it adds

Write ordinary Markdown: `#` headings, paragraphs, `- ` and `1. ` lists nested by two spaces, `- [ ]` and `- [x]` tasks, `> ` quotes, `---` rules, tables with a `--- | ---` line under their header row, and inline `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `~~strike~~`, `[words](https://…)`. A footnote sits where it belongs: `^[the note's words]` (Markdown's `[^1]` with a `[^1]: the note` paragraph reads too). TLO adds:

| Write | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `---` / `key: value` lines / `---` at the very top | The head: the document's settings (`chart: bar`, `zone: Europe/London`, `theme: midnight`) and its `title` and `by` |
| `{#id .class key=value}` at the end of a line | Attributes: a layout (`{.title}`, `{.two}`), a setting for that line (`{due=2027-03-01}`) |
| `Price:money` in a table's header | A typed column: `text number money percent date time check url rich long icon name option` |
| `~ A -> B: label` | A connection between two things (`->`, `<-`, `<->`, `--`) |
| a code fence named for an app: ```` ```sheet ```` | Another document inside this one, written in that app's TLO: a chart on a slide, a table in a text |
| `==highlight==`, `++underline++`, `:icon-name:` | A highlight, an underline, an icon in the line (Lucide's names: `rocket`, `calendar`, `coffee`…) |

`---` between blocks starts the next slide, page or card. A table anywhere is a spreadsheet: its formulas work. A link is words: `[words](https://…)` or a web address, alone on a line or among other words, is words that go there when the reader follows them. Nothing in a document is fetched from another site: there are no pictures from the web and no embedded videos or posts, and Markdown's picture line, `![words](https://…)`, reads as a link.

## The apps

| App | Name | For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `write` | Word Processor | Words on a page: headings, lists, links and notes, a table that adds up, printed on letter or A4. |
| `outline` | Outliner | An outliner: ideas under ideas, folded and unfolded, moved about and joined; the same tree a deck or a mind map reads. |
| `deck` | Presentation Builder | Slides: titles, bullets, two columns, big icons, other documents on a slide; or a zine, booklet, brochure, comic, poster or name badges to print and fold. |
| `sheet` | Spreadsheet | A spreadsheet with formulas, named cells and charts; three columns to start, more as you need them. |
| `calc` | Calculator | A calculator that keeps its working: names, units and conversions, and graphs of y = f(x). |
| `draw` | Drawing Tool | Boxes, arrows, icons and labels on a grid; or pixel art, which can become a background tile. |
| `diagram` | Diagram Maker | Mind maps, org charts, family trees, swimlanes, timelines, Venns, seating charts and networks, drawn from a few lines. |
| `anim` | Animator | Anything from the Drawing Tool, moving: position, depth, size, spin and turn over time, with effects for memes. |
| `cal` | Calendar | Days and times on a month, a year or a schedule, in any time zone. |
| `trip` | Trip Planner | A route on a map: stops in order, each with a note, and how far between them. |

## Words

### write: a text

Markdown as it stands. `# Words {.title}` is the title, set large; `#` and `##` are headings; `{.center}`, `{.right}` or `{.justify}` at the end of a paragraph aligns it. A table works out its formulas; a fence named for an app holds that document. `paper: a4` or `letter` in the head sets the paper (a reader in North America gets letter otherwise). Notes are listed at the end, in the editor, on paper, in the web page and in Word. an invoice is a text with its lines as a table.

Meeting notes:

```
# Meeting {.title}

*The date · where · who came*

## Agenda

1. *First item*
2. *Second item*

## Notes

*What was said, briefly.*

## Decisions

- *What was decided.*

## Actions

- [ ] *Who does what, by when*
```

As a link: <https://tinylittleoffice.com/write/#doc=%23+Meeting+%7B.title%7D%0A%0A%2AThe+date+%C2%B7+where+%C2%B7+who+came%2A%0A%0A%23%23+Agenda%0A%0A1.+%2AFirst+item%2A%0A2.+%2ASecond+item%2A%0A%0A%23%23+Notes%0A%0A%2AWhat+was+said%2C+briefly.%2A%0A%0A%23%23+Decisions%0A%0A-+%2AWhat+was+decided.%2A%0A%0A%23%23+Actions%0A%0A-+%5B+%5D+%2AWho+does+what%2C+by+when%2A>

Templates: A letter, Cover letter, Memo, Meeting notes, Minutes, Résumé, One-page CV, Invoice, Contract, Newsletter, Recipe, Questions and answers, Press release, News article, Interview, Book review, Music review, Thesis, Grant proposal, Syllabus, Formal complaint, Letter to a politician, Love letter, Wedding speech, Eulogy, Zine essay, Petition, Terms of service. Its own files: `.docx`, `.md`, `.rtf`, `.html`.

### outline: an outliner

A nested list, two spaces a level. An item's tie to its parent can be an arrow, `{.to}` (towards the parent) or `{.from}`, named with `label="…"`; any two items join with `~ Pricing -> Press: informs`. The same tree opens as slides, a mind map, an org chart or a network.

Launch plan:

```
---
title: Fieldnote 2.0 launch
---
- Fieldnote 2.0, out on Thursday 12 November
  - Product
    - Pricing {.from label=sets}
      - £4 a month or £36 a year; free for students^[Three rivals checked in September: £3 to £6 a month.]
    - Onboarding
      - Three screens, then straight to the first note
    - Freeze the build on Monday 2 November
  - Marketing
    - Press
      - Review copies to six writers on 5 November, embargoed to the 12th
    - Newsletter
      - To 4,200 readers at 8 am on launch day
    - A ninety-second film of a note being made
  - Support
    - Help pages
      - Twelve of them, the five most asked about first
    - A reply within a day, Priya and Tom taking turns

~ Pricing -> Press: informs
~ Help pages -> Newsletter: linked from
```

As a link: <https://tinylittleoffice.com/outline/#doc=---%0Atitle%3A+Fieldnote+2.0+launch%0A---%0A-+Fieldnote+2.0%2C+out+on+Thursday+12+November%0A++-+Product%0A++++-+Pricing+%7B.from+label%3Dsets%7D%0A++++++-+%C2%A34+a+month+or+%C2%A336+a+year%3B+free+for+students%5E%5BThree+rivals+checked+in+September%3A+%C2%A33+to+%C2%A36+a+month.%5D%0A++++-+Onboarding%0A++++++-+Three+screens%2C+then+straight+to+the+first+note%0A++++-+Freeze+the+build+on+Monday+2+November%0A++-+Marketing%0A++++-+Press%0A++++++-+Review+copies+to+six+writers+on+5+November%2C+embargoed+to+the+12th%0A++++-+Newsletter%0A++++++-+To+4%2C200+readers+at+8+am+on+launch+day%0A++++-+A+ninety-second+film+of+a+note+being+made%0A++-+Support%0A++++-+Help+pages%0A++++++-+Twelve+of+them%2C+the+five+most+asked+about+first%0A++++-+A+reply+within+a+day%2C+Priya+and+Tom+taking+turns%0A%0A~+Pricing+-%3E+Press%3A+informs%0A~+Help+pages+-%3E+Newsletter%3A+linked+from>

Templates: Packing list, A decision, Launch plan, A talk, A speech, An essay plan, A research plan, A syllabus, A novel, A book, A company, A family, A decision tree, Troubleshooting. Its own files: `.opml`, `.md`, `.pdf`, `.txt`. (the `.pdf` is the outline's words as sections and bullets, selectable and bookmarked)

## Slides and things to print

### deck: slides

A slide between each `---`. The headline is `## :icon-name: Headline`, its layout an attribute: `{.title}` (a title slide), `{.two}` (two columns, a paragraph `|` between them) or `{.icon}` (bullets beside one big icon). The words are `- ` bullets nested by two spaces; `> ` lines are speaker notes; a `^[footnote]` is shown at the foot of its slide. A sheet's table with `chart: bar` in its head, in a ```` ```sheet ```` fence, is a chart on the slide. The head may hold `theme:` (`boardroom`, `ivory`, `midnight`, `graphite`; for fun `confetti`, `sunset`, `ocean`, `bubblegum`, `arcade`, `chalkboard`; plain otherwise) and `transition:` (`cut`, `slide`, `zoom`; a fade otherwise).

The rules, before they are broken: a slide with a fence (a chart, a diagram, a table) is the fence's, drawn alone under the headline: bullets on it are not drawn, so put them in the notes (`> ` lines) or on a slide of their own. A headline is a few words; a long one is set smaller, then cut after two lines. Bullets are set as large as they fit, down to 14px; more than that runs off the slide, so split it. Presenting reveals one bullet, or one item of a fenced document, per step; the notes show with N or the Notes button, and start hidden under a finger. `{.title}` is a cover (the headline large, the bullets beneath it as its subtitle); `{.two}` two columns, `|` alone on a line between them; `{.icon}` the bullets beside the headline's icon, drawn large.

`format:` in the head makes the deck a thing to print and fold, a page between each `---`: `poster` (one page, as big as the page allows), `zine` (8 pages), `booklet` (8 to 20), `brochure` (6 panels), `comic` (a panel per bullet, `- :icon-name: What is said | caption`) or `badges` (a page per person, the name as the headline).

Status update:

```
---
theme: boardroom
---
## :calendar: Acme Ltd site: status {.title}

- Week of 2 November 2026 · Harbor Studio

---

## This week and next {.two}

- Done: the six pages sketched and agreed
- Done: words for home, about and contact
- Done: hosting set up, the old address kept

|

- Next: words for work, prices and news
- Next: photographs on Thursday morning, weather allowing
- Next: first build shown on Friday 13 November

> Left, what shipped; right, what is planned. Keep it to the facts.

---

## :warning: Risks

- The price list is still being decided by Acme: the prices page waits on it
- Thursday may rain: Saturday is the fallback for photographs

---

## :help: Asks

- Dee Okafor to send the final prices by Wednesday 11 November
- Someone from Acme at the Friday read-through, an hour
```

As a link: <https://tinylittleoffice.com/deck/#doc=---%0Atheme%3A+boardroom%0A---%0A%23%23+%3Acalendar%3A+Acme+Ltd+site%3A+status+%7B.title%7D%0A%0A-+Week+of+2+November+2026+%C2%B7+Harbor+Studio%0A%0A---%0A%0A%23%23+This+week+and+next+%7B.two%7D%0A%0A-+Done%3A+the+six+pages+sketched+and+agreed%0A-+Done%3A+words+for+home%2C+about+and+contact%0A-+Done%3A+hosting+set+up%2C+the+old+address+kept%0A%0A%7C%0A%0A-+Next%3A+words+for+work%2C+prices+and+news%0A-+Next%3A+photographs+on+Thursday+morning%2C+weather+allowing%0A-+Next%3A+first+build+shown+on+Friday+13+November%0A%0A%3E+Left%2C+what+shipped%3B+right%2C+what+is+planned.+Keep+it+to+the+facts.%0A%0A---%0A%0A%23%23+%3Awarning%3A+Risks%0A%0A-+The+price+list+is+still+being+decided+by+Acme%3A+the+prices+page+waits+on+it%0A-+Thursday+may+rain%3A+Saturday+is+the+fallback+for+photographs%0A%0A---%0A%0A%23%23+%3Ahelp%3A+Asks%0A%0A-+Dee+Okafor+to+send+the+final+prices+by+Wednesday+11+November%0A-+Someone+from+Acme+at+the+Friday+read-through%2C+an+hour>

Templates: A talk, Status update, A proposal, A pitch, A lesson, Conference talk, Quarterly review, Workshop agenda, Product launch, Town-hall notice, Trivia night, Wedding slideshow, Zine, Recipe zine, Booklet, Concert programme, Brochure, Farm brochure, Comic, Comic: the umbrella, Poster, Lost cat poster, Name badges, Conference badges. Its own files: `.pptx`, `.html`, `.zip`, `.gif`.

## Numbers

### sheet: a spreadsheet, a chart, a model

One table. Its header row names the columns, each optionally typed (`Sales:money`); the rows under it are rows 1, 2, 3, so `=SUM(B1:B3)` adds the first three. Up to 26 columns (A to Z). A cell starting with `=` is a formula: `+ - * / ^`, comparisons, references (`B2`), ranges (`A1:A5`), and these functions: `SUM`, `AVG`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `COUNT`, `SUMIF`, `COUNTIF`, `MEDIAN`, `PRODUCT`, `IF`, `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, `ROUND`, `ROUNDUP`, `ROUNDDOWN`, `INT`, `ABS`, `SQRT`, `MOD`, `NPV`, `IRR`, `PMT`, `FV`, `PV`, `TODAY`, `DATE`, `DAYS`, `EDATE`, `WORKDAYS`, `YEAR`, `MONTH`, `DAY`, `WEEKDAY`. Dates are written `2027-03-01` in a `date` column. `chart: bar` (or `line`, `pie`) in the head draws the first column's labels against the numbers beside them; `chart: sankey` draws rows of `From | To | Amount` as flows.

A model is a sheet: a column typed `name` names the cell to its right, and formulas use the names (`=visitors*signup_rate/100`; a space is `_`); `lock: C1:C6` in the head marks the model's own formulas, so a reader changes the assumptions and not the model.

Budget:

```
---
title: Budget, October 2026
---
Item | Planned:money | Actual:money | Difference:money
--- | --- | --- | ---
Rent | 1200 | 1200 | =C1-B1
Groceries | 500 | 540 | =C2-B2
Transport | 150 | 120 | =C3-B3
Utilities | 180 | 175 | =C4-B4
Fun | 200 | 260 | =C5-B5
Savings | 400 | 400 | =C6-B6
Total | =SUM(B1:B6) | =SUM(C1:C6) | =SUM(D1:D6)
```

As a link: <https://tinylittleoffice.com/sheet/#doc=---%0Atitle%3A+Budget%2C+October+2026%0A---%0AItem+%7C+Planned%3Amoney+%7C+Actual%3Amoney+%7C+Difference%3Amoney%0A---+%7C+---+%7C+---+%7C+---%0ARent+%7C+1200+%7C+1200+%7C+%3DC1-B1%0AGroceries+%7C+500+%7C+540+%7C+%3DC2-B2%0ATransport+%7C+150+%7C+120+%7C+%3DC3-B3%0AUtilities+%7C+180+%7C+175+%7C+%3DC4-B4%0AFun+%7C+200+%7C+260+%7C+%3DC5-B5%0ASavings+%7C+400+%7C+400+%7C+%3DC6-B6%0ATotal+%7C+%3DSUM%28B1%3AB6%29+%7C+%3DSUM%28C1%3AC6%29+%7C+%3DSUM%28D1%3AD6%29>

A subscription business:

```
---
title: A subscription business, a month
chart: sankey
lock: C1:C6, E6:E9
---
From | To | Amount:number | Assumption:name | Value:number
--- | --- | --- | --- | ---
Visitors | Signups | =visitors*signup_rate/100 | Visitors | 20000
Visitors | Bounced | =visitors-signups | Signup rate | 6
Signups | Paying | =signups*paid_rate/100 | Paid rate | 25
Signups | Free | =signups-paying | Churn | 8
Paying | Churned | =paying*churn/100 |  |
Paying | Retained | =paying-churned | Signups | =SUMIF(B1:B20, "Signups", C1:C20)
| |  |  | Paying | =SUMIF(B1:B20, "Paying", C1:C20)
| |  |  | Churned | =SUMIF(B1:B20, "Churned", C1:C20)
| |  |  | Retained | =SUMIF(B1:B20, "Retained", C1:C20)
{big=Retained}
```

As a link: <https://tinylittleoffice.com/sheet/#doc=---%0Atitle%3A+A+subscription+business%2C+a+month%0Achart%3A+sankey%0Alock%3A+C1%3AC6%2C+E6%3AE9%0A---%0AFrom+%7C+To+%7C+Amount%3Anumber+%7C+Assumption%3Aname+%7C+Value%3Anumber%0A---+%7C+---+%7C+---+%7C+---+%7C+---%0AVisitors+%7C+Signups+%7C+%3Dvisitors%2Asignup_rate%2F100+%7C+Visitors+%7C+20000%0AVisitors+%7C+Bounced+%7C+%3Dvisitors-signups+%7C+Signup+rate+%7C+6%0ASignups+%7C+Paying+%7C+%3Dsignups%2Apaid_rate%2F100+%7C+Paid+rate+%7C+25%0ASignups+%7C+Free+%7C+%3Dsignups-paying+%7C+Churn+%7C+8%0APaying+%7C+Churned+%7C+%3Dpaying%2Achurn%2F100+%7C++%7C%0APaying+%7C+Retained+%7C+%3Dpaying-churned+%7C+Signups+%7C+%3DSUMIF%28B1%3AB20%2C+%22Signups%22%2C+C1%3AC20%29%0A%7C+%7C++%7C++%7C+Paying+%7C+%3DSUMIF%28B1%3AB20%2C+%22Paying%22%2C+C1%3AC20%29%0A%7C+%7C++%7C++%7C+Churned+%7C+%3DSUMIF%28B1%3AB20%2C+%22Churned%22%2C+C1%3AC20%29%0A%7C+%7C++%7C++%7C+Retained+%7C+%3DSUMIF%28B1%3AB20%2C+%22Retained%22%2C+C1%3AC20%29%0A%7Bbig%3DRetained%7D>

Templates: Budget, Household budget by month, Expense log, Savings goal, Habit tracker, Reading list, Workout log, Training log, Time sheet, Trip costs split, Project tracker, Schedule with dates, Grade book, Membership roll, Seating count, Poll results, Fundraising thermometer, Invoice ledger, Inventory, Petty cash, Rate card, Mortgages compared, Loans compared, Unit converter, Tournament bracket, Month by month, with a chart, A subscription business, A café, A freelancer, A mutual aid fund. Its own files: `.xlsx`, `.csv`, `.chart.svg`, `.chart.png`.

### calc: a calculator that keeps its working

An expression a line (`2+3*4`, `sqrt(16)`, `20!`); `name = expression` keeps its answer under that name for the lines after it, and `ans` is the line before. Units convert (`3 inch to cm`, `60 mph in km/h`). `mode: graph` in the head draws each line as a curve y = f(x), with `x from 0 to 400` setting the range.

Splitting the bill:

```
---
title: Dinner for six
---
food = 164.50
drinks = 58
tip = (food + drinks) * 18%
total = food + drinks + tip
total / 6
```

As a link: <https://tinylittleoffice.com/calc/#doc=---%0Atitle%3A+Dinner+for+six%0A---%0Afood+%3D+164.50%0Adrinks+%3D+58%0Atip+%3D+%28food+%2B+drinks%29+%2A+18%25%0Atotal+%3D+food+%2B+drinks+%2B+tip%0Atotal+%2F+6>

Templates: Splitting the bill, A shopping total, Tax on a price, Percentage change, Kitchen conversions, Scaling a recipe, Unit conversions, Currency at a rate you type, Fuel for a trip, Paint for a room, Time zones, Running pace, Body mass index, Dose by weight, Electricity for an appliance, Loan payment, Compound interest, Break-even, A curve and its slope, Waves adding up. Its own files: `.txt`.

## Pictures

### draw: a drawing, or pixel art

A table `Kind | X | Y | W | H | Style | Label`, a row per shape, on a grid of 8px squares. Kinds: `r` rectangle, `o` rounded box, `e` ellipse, `d` diamond, `h` hexagon, `p` parallelogram, `c` cylinder, `n` note, `t` text, `i` icon (its label is the icon's name), `l` line, `a` arrow (X, Y the start; W, H the distance to the end). `k` joins two shapes with an arrow and `j` with a line: their X and Y are the row numbers (from 0) of the shapes joined. Style is a fill (`0` none, `1` tint, `2` solid), then a colour letter (`r o g b p`) and a text size (`1` to `4`); a text (`t`) may end it with `=` to centre its words or `>` to set them right. `alt:` in the head describes the drawing for people who cannot see it. Prefer a diagram when one fits: it lays itself out.

Request flow:

```
---
title: How a page loads
alt: A browser asks a server, which reads the data.
---
Kind | X | Y | W | H | Style | Label
--- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---
o | 4 | 6 | 16 | 8 | 1b | Browser
o | 32 | 6 | 16 | 8 | 1b | Server
c | 60 | 5 | 14 | 10 | 1g | Data
k | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | asks
k | 1 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | reads
```

As a link: <https://tinylittleoffice.com/draw/#doc=---%0Atitle%3A+How+a+page+loads%0Aalt%3A+A+browser+asks+a+server%2C+which+reads+the+data.%0A---%0AKind+%7C+X+%7C+Y+%7C+W+%7C+H+%7C+Style+%7C+Label%0A---+%7C+---+%7C+---+%7C+---+%7C+---+%7C+---+%7C+---%0Ao+%7C+4+%7C+6+%7C+16+%7C+8+%7C+1b+%7C+Browser%0Ao+%7C+32+%7C+6+%7C+16+%7C+8+%7C+1b+%7C+Server%0Ac+%7C+60+%7C+5+%7C+14+%7C+10+%7C+1g+%7C+Data%0Ak+%7C+0+%7C+1+%7C+0+%7C+0+%7C+0+%7C+asks%0Ak+%7C+1+%7C+2+%7C+0+%7C+0+%7C+0+%7C+reads>

Pixel art: `grid: 16` (or 8, 32, 64) in the head, then a line per row and a letter per square, `.` clear and `a` to `h` the inks.

Pixel heart:

```
---
title: A heart
grid: 16
---
....cc....cc....
...cccc..cccc...
..cccccccccccc..
..chccccccccccc.
..chccccccccccc.
..cccccccccccc..
...cccccccccc...
....cccccccc....
.....cccccc.....
......cccc......
.......cc.......
```

As a link: <https://tinylittleoffice.com/draw/#doc=---%0Atitle%3A+A+heart%0Agrid%3A+16%0A---%0A....cc....cc....%0A...cccc..cccc...%0A..cccccccccccc..%0A..chccccccccccc.%0A..chccccccccccc.%0A..cccccccccccc..%0A...cccccccccc...%0A....cccccccc....%0A.....cccccc.....%0A......cccc......%0A.......cc.......>

Templates: Flowchart, Birthday card, Event map, Floor plan, Room plan, Wireframe, Logo sketch, Badge, Order to doorstep, Request flow, Three tiers, Pixel heart, Weather icons, Game sprite, Background tile. Its own files: `.svg`, `.tile.svg`, `.tile.png`.

### diagram: a diagram drawn from a few lines

`kind:` in the head says which, and each is a list:

- `mind`: a nested list, the centre then its branches.
- `org`: a nested list of `Name | Role`; a dotted line between two people is `~ Ben -- Eve: advises`.
- `family`: a nested list, a person or a couple each, `Rose + Albert Hale | m. 1948`.
- `lanes`: `- Who: what they do`, in order; a step ending in `?` is a decision.
- `timeline`: `- When: what happened`; dates or years are spaced as they fell, and a span (`- 2027-02-01 – 2027-08-02: Builders on site`) is a band.
- `venn`: `- Set: thing, thing` for two or three sets, `- A & B: thing` for what they share.
- `seating`: `- Table: Ann, Bob, Cy`.
- `net`: `~ A -> B: label` connections; `- name` a thing on its own.

What each is good for: `mind` ideas branching from one, `org` who reports to whom, `family` generations, `lanes` a process passed between people, `timeline` dates spaced as they fell, `venn` what two or three sets share, `seating` who sits where, `net` what talks to what.

The rules, before they are broken: a thing is a name, short (two to four words; a box holds no more), and its other words go in a child, in a connection's label, or in the notes. A connection's ends are names in the list, written exactly as the line writes them (the words before ` | `); in a tree an end naming no thing is not drawn, and a network makes a second thing of it. In a `net` a line is one thing named by the whole line: `- Header: the logo` is a thing called "Header: the logo", so write `- Header` and put "the logo" in a label. In `venn` and `seating` a comma separates things, a comma in a number too: "2,000 cases" is two things, so write 2000 or two thousand. A label is a few words: longer ones lie over each other. `lanes`, `timeline`, `venn` and `seating` draw no connections.

A small company:

```
---
title: Who reports to whom
kind: org
---
- Ada Diaz | Chief executive
  - Ben Okoro | Engineering
    - Cy Lund | Platform
    - Di Shah | Apps
  - Eve Marsh | Design
  - Flo Reyes | Sales
    - Gus Patel | Accounts

~ Cy Lund -- Eve Marsh: design partner
```

As a link: <https://tinylittleoffice.com/diagram/#doc=---%0Atitle%3A+Who+reports+to+whom%0Akind%3A+org%0A---%0A-+Ada+Diaz+%7C+Chief+executive%0A++-+Ben+Okoro+%7C+Engineering%0A++++-+Cy+Lund+%7C+Platform%0A++++-+Di+Shah+%7C+Apps%0A++-+Eve+Marsh+%7C+Design%0A++-+Flo+Reyes+%7C+Sales%0A++++-+Gus+Patel+%7C+Accounts%0A%0A~+Cy+Lund+--+Eve+Marsh%3A+design+partner>

Cats and dogs:

```
---
title: Cats and dogs
kind: venn
---
- Cats: purr, climb curtains, use a litter tray
- Dogs: fetch, need walks, guard the house
- Cats & Dogs: shed on the sofa, love a warm spot, wake you at six
```

As a link: <https://tinylittleoffice.com/diagram/#doc=---%0Atitle%3A+Cats+and+dogs%0Akind%3A+venn%0A---%0A-+Cats%3A+purr%2C+climb+curtains%2C+use+a+litter+tray%0A-+Dogs%3A+fetch%2C+need+walks%2C+guard+the+house%0A-+Cats+%26+Dogs%3A+shed+on+the+sofa%2C+love+a+warm+spot%2C+wake+you+at+six>

Templates: Mind map, Launch plan, The garden this year, Moving abroad, Revising for an exam, Org chart, A small company, A primary school, A restaurant kitchen, Family tree, Three generations, The Brontës, A family with a godmother, Swimlanes, From order to doorstep, Hiring someone, An expenses claim, Timeline, Computing, briefly, A building project, Apollo 11, Venn, Fast, cheap, good, Cats and dogs, Who can do what, Seating chart, A wedding dinner, Board game night, A classroom, Network, How an app hangs together, The water cycle, The house network. Its own files: `.svg`.

### anim: a drawing that moves

A drawing's table, then a table `Shape | Keys`: for each moving shape (its row number from 0), keys separated by `; `, each `frame,dx,dy,depth,size,spin[,effects]`: where it is at that frame as an offset in pixels from where it was drawn, its depth (nearer when positive), its size as a scale (1 as drawn), its spin in degrees, and effect letters (`i` impact, `3` 3D, `d` shadow, `n` neon, `o` outline, `g` rainbow, `m` mirror, `w` wobble, `b` blur). Between keys it moves in straight lines. The head holds `frames` (2 to 120), `fps` (1 to 30) and `loop` (`once`, a number, or `bounce`; for ever otherwise).

Lift off:

```
---
title: Lift off
frames: 24
fps: 8
alt: A rocket lifts off and flies up and away to the right, under the words Lift off.
---
Kind | X | Y | W | H | Style | Label
--- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | ---
t | 4 | 20 | 20 | 4 | 04 | Lift off
i | 8 | 36 | 8 | 8 | 0b | rocket

Shape | Keys
--- | ---
0 | 0,0,0,0,1,0; 23,0,-80,0,1,0,i
1 | 0,0,0,0,1,0; 23,200,-200,80,1,-30,d
```

As a link: <https://tinylittleoffice.com/anim/#doc=---%0Atitle%3A+Lift+off%0Aframes%3A+24%0Afps%3A+8%0Aalt%3A+A+rocket+lifts+off+and+flies+up+and+away+to+the+right%2C+under+the+words+Lift+off.%0A---%0AKind+%7C+X+%7C+Y+%7C+W+%7C+H+%7C+Style+%7C+Label%0A---+%7C+---+%7C+---+%7C+---+%7C+---+%7C+---+%7C+---%0At+%7C+4+%7C+20+%7C+20+%7C+4+%7C+04+%7C+Lift+off%0Ai+%7C+8+%7C+36+%7C+8+%7C+8+%7C+0b+%7C+rocket%0A%0AShape+%7C+Keys%0A---+%7C+---%0A0+%7C+0%2C0%2C0%2C0%2C1%2C0%3B+23%2C0%2C-80%2C0%2C1%2C0%2Ci%0A1+%7C+0%2C0%2C0%2C0%2C1%2C0%3B+23%2C200%2C-200%2C80%2C1%2C-30%2Cd>

Templates: Lift off, Bouncing ball, Loading spinner, Title card, Birthday card, Quick standup, Build is green, Flash card, Weather this week, New Year countdown, Flight path, Neon sign, Sunrise. Its own files: `.gif`, `.svg`.

## Plans

### cal: a calendar, or a schedule

A list item per thing: `- 2027-03-01: Launch`, `- 2027-03-01 to 2027-03-03: Offsite`, `- 2027-03-10 09:00-10:30: Retro`. Attributes give a colour and a repeat: `{color=green every=week times=6}` (or `until=2027-06-01`). The head holds the time zone, `zone: Europe/London`, and may say what a colour stands for: `green: Sam`. `view: gantt` in the head draws the same items as a schedule: an item nested under another is part of it, `{done=40%}` is how far along it is, `- [x]` that it is done.

Family calendar:

```
---
title: The Okafor family
zone: Europe/London
green: Sam
orange: Ana
blue: Everyone
---
- 2026-11-03 16:30-17:15: Swimming lesson, Sam {color=green every=week times=10}
- 2026-11-04: Bins out, garden waste too {every=week}
- 2026-11-05 18:30-20:00: Bonfire night at Victoria Park, bring gloves {color=blue}
- 2026-11-07 10:00-11:30: Football, under-10s home game {color=green every=week until=2026-12-12}
- 2026-11-09: Ana's birthday {color=orange every=year}
- 2026-11-12 08:40-09:20: Dentist, Dr Patel, both children {color=blue}
- 2026-11-21 to 2026-11-22: Grandma visits from Leeds {color=blue}
- 2026-11-26 19:30-22:00: Book club at Jo's {color=orange every=month}
- 2026-12-19 to 2027-01-04: Christmas holidays {color=green}
```

### trip: a route on a map

A table `Place | Lat:number | Lon:number | Note`, in decimal degrees. `units: km` or `units: miles` in the head (driving hours are estimated otherwise); `route: dots` for places that stand alone, not a route.

A week in Portugal:

```
---
units: km
---
Place | Lat:number | Lon:number | Note
--- | --- | --- | ---
Lisbon | 38.7223 | -9.1393 | Pastéis de nata in Belém, then the 28 tram up to Graça
Sintra | 38.8029 | -9.3817 | Pena Palace first thing, before the coaches
Óbidos | 39.3606 | -9.1571 | Walk the town walls; ginjinha in a chocolate cup
Coimbra | 40.2033 | -8.4103 | The Joanina Library: book the 10:00 slot
Porto | 41.1579 | -8.6291 | Port cellars across the river in Gaia
```

## Every app's files

Every document downloads as a `.pdf` (its pages as pictures; Print in the browser saves one with the words still words), a picture (`.png`), a web page (`.html`), Markdown (`.md`, footnotes in Markdown's reference form) and its own text (`.tlo`: the TLO with `app: <id>` in its head, which opens as its own app when dropped on the site or opened from its menu). A `.zip` of `.tlo` and `.md` files, a folder per app as the site's Download everything writes it, opens the same way: every document in it is kept on the device (under Private, listed to keep or to open). A link that downloads a file as it opens is `#/v1/<app>.<ext>/<payload>`, or `view=<ext>` in the plain form.

## Short links

The API below is this site's. Make a short link at the shortener of the site the link opens on, `tinier.<the site's host>`: the shortener opens only links to its own site. An agent on a development machine running its own copy of the site uses that site's `/tinier/` (the shortener started with `SITE` set to the site's address, `npm run tinier:dev`), and the link it makes opens there; production's shortener accepts only links to production.

A long link can be shortened at tinier.tinylittleoffice.com for an hour, a day, a week or a month. The link is encrypted where it is made (AES-256-GCM, a random key); only the ciphertext goes to the service, and the key travels in the short link's fragment, which browsers never send. A program can do the same:

```
POST https://tinier.tinylittleoffice.com/api   {c, iv, ttl}   → 201 {id, exp}
```

`c` and `iv` are the AES-GCM ciphertext of the long link and its 12-byte IV, base64url; `ttl` is 3600, 86400, 604800 or 2592000 seconds (a month at most). The short link is `https://tinier.tinylittleoffice.com/<id>#<key>` (the key as base64url). A short link cannot be changed or recalled once made; it expires on its own, so make a new one for a new version. The ciphertext may be 16 KiB at most, and one address may make a hundred links a day (the 101st is 429, with `Retry-After`).

## Who made it

The head may carry `created` (when the document was first written, to the minute) and `by` (who made it, a claim: nothing proves it). Write `by` to say who you are.

## Without a browser

The site serves its own API as a module, for programs and agents; nothing to install:

```js
import { link, plain, read, compare, apps, templates } from 'https://tinylittleoffice.com/api.js';
const url = link('sheet', 'Item | Cost:money\n--- | ---\nRent | 1200\n', { title: 'Budget', by: 'planner-agent' });
read(url).text;                 // the document's TLO text, its title and by in the head
compare(url, revised).changes;  // what the second link changed, block by block
await templates('deck');        // what a deck can start from
```

A link opens in its reader's browser's language; `link(app, text, { lang: 'ht' })` (or `--lang ht`) makes one that opens in Haitian Creole, or any language the site has (`es`, `pt-br`, `zh-hant`, …), whatever the reader's browser says.

A page of your own can import `https://tinylittleoffice.com/tinyoffice.js` instead: `link({ app, doc, title })` writes the plain link and `embed({ app, doc, title })` the `<iframe>` that shows the document's pages. In the API, `encode`/`decode` are the codec, `parse`/`write` the kernel (the document as a head and blocks, and back), `tlo`/`fromTlo` a `.tlo` file's text, `file(app, text, ext)` a file of the app's own formats that needs no browser. In a clone of github.com/aboard-io/tinylittleoffice, `node packages/doc/tinyoffice.ts` is the same from the command line: `link`, `read`, `file`, `diff`, `lint`, `measure`, `apps`, `templates`.

## Check it, do not look at it

Before you share a link, lint it: `tinyoffice lint <link or file.tlo>` (or `await lint(app, text)` in the API). It says what a reader's eye would have seen, a line a finding, `app · slide or block · the finding · what to do`, and exits 1 when there is one; `--json` gives `{findings: [{app, at, block, kind, words, fix}]}`. The findings:

- `edge-end`: a connection names a thing that is not in the list (a tree draws it not at all).
- `edge-unused`: a connection in a kind that draws none.
- `net-colon`: a network's `- Name: description` line, named by the whole line.
- `comma-number`: a comma inside a number in a Venn's or a table's list, cutting it in two.
- `label-long`: a thing's words too long for its box: set at the smallest size, or cut with "…".
- `label-over`: a connection's label lying over another label or a thing's words.
- `fence-bullets`: bullets on a slide that shows a document, not drawn.
- `title-cut`, `title-small`: a headline cut after two lines, or set at its smallest size.
- `body-over`, `body-small`: a slide's words running off its foot, or set at their smallest size.
- `formula-error`: a table's formula that works out to an error (`#CIRC`, `#REF`, `#DIV/0`, `#NAME`, `#VALUE`, `#NUM`, `#ERR`), in any table, a fenced one too: the cell, the formula, the error and the fix. A total over its own column takes in its own cell when the rows are counted from the header: rows count from the first data row, so the eighth row's total of the seven above is `=SUM(B1:B7)`.
- `length`: a link past 2,000 characters, which some chat apps cut.

A diagram fenced on a slide is linted too, at its slide. `tinyoffice measure <link or file>` (`measure(app, text)`) gives the numbers behind them as JSON: per slide, the headline's and the words' sizes, the lines they wrapped to, what was cut and the bullets a document hides, what it shows (`shows`); per diagram, its things, its connections drawn and dropped, and each label's size, lines and whether it was cut; per table, its formulas and the ones that fail. Set your words from these numbers. `read` gives back the text exactly as written, so what you wrote is what the link holds. You never need a browser or a screenshot to check a document: the lint and the measures come from the same layout code that draws the pages. If you do open a development copy of the site, short links need its shortener (`npm run tinier:dev`).

## Driving the editors

For an agent working in the editors in a browser: the keys each app answers, written from the apps' command registry (`Mod` is ⌘ on a Mac and Ctrl elsewhere; `at:` places are inside the app). Every command in force is also in the command palette, Mod+K (outside words) or the button at the end of the bar.

- **Everywhere (the page)**: `Mod+Z` Undo; `Mod+Shift+Z`/`Mod+Y` Redo; `Mod+F` Find in this document; `Mod+S` Keep this document on the device; `Mod+Shift+S` Share; `Mod+Shift+D` Download; `Mod+P` Print, or save as PDF; `Mod+/` Show these shortcuts; `Mod+K` All commands.
- **Words (wherever words are typed)**: `Mod+X` Cut; `Mod+C` Copy; `Mod+V` Paste; `Mod+B` Bold; `Mod+I` Italic; `Mod+U` Underline; `Mod+Shift+X` Strikethrough; `Mod+Shift+H` Highlight; `Mod+K` Link; `Tab` Indent; `Shift+Tab` Bring out; `Alt+ArrowUp` Move up; `Alt+ArrowDown` Move down; `Mod+Enter` Tick or untick a task; `Mod+A` Select all: the words of the box, then everything.
- **Rows chosen whole**: `Enter` Edit; `Escape` Step out: close, collapse, let go; `Alt+ArrowUp` Move up; `Alt+ArrowDown` Move down; `Tab` Indent; `Shift+Tab` Bring out; `Mod+D` Duplicate; `Mod+C` Copy; `Mod+X` Cut; `Mod+V` Paste; `Delete`/`Backspace` Delete; `Shift+ArrowUp`/`Shift+ArrowDown` Extend the selection; `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`/`ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` Back to the words; `Mod+A` Select all: the words of the box, then everything.
- **Word Processor**: `Mod+Shift+Enter` Page break; `Mod+Shift+L` Align left; `Mod+Shift+E` Centre; `Mod+Shift+R` Align right; `Mod+Shift+J` Justify; `Enter` Edit; `Alt+ArrowUp` Move up; `Alt+ArrowDown` Move down; `Mod+D` Duplicate; `Mod+C` Copy; `Mod+X` Cut; `Mod+V` Paste; `Delete`/`Backspace` Delete; `Escape`/`ArrowDown`/`ArrowRight` Back to the words; `ArrowUp`/`ArrowLeft` Back to the words.
- **Outliner**: `Tab` Indent; `Shift+Tab` Bring out; `Alt+ArrowUp` Move up; `Alt+ArrowDown` Move down; `Mod+Shift+,` Zoom out; `Mod+Shift+.` Zoom in; `Mod+Alt+ArrowUp`/`Mod+Alt+ArrowDown` Fold, unfold; `Mod+D` Duplicate; `Delete`/`Backspace` Delete; `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`/`ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` The next or the one before.
- **Presentation Builder**: `Mod+Alt+Enter` Present; `Alt+ArrowUp` Move slide up; `Alt+ArrowDown` Move slide down; `Mod+Shift+Enter` A new slide; `Mod+Enter` Done; `Mod+D` Duplicate; `PageUp`/`PageDown` The slide before, the slide after (on the rail); `ArrowRight`/`Space`/`PageDown`/`Enter` Presenting: the next line or slide; `ArrowLeft`/`PageUp`/`Backspace` Presenting: back; `End` Presenting: the whole slide; `N`/`Shift+N` Notes; `Escape` Stop presenting.
- **Spreadsheet**: `Mod+Alt+=` Row above; `Mod+D` Fill down from the top row; `Mod+C` Copy; `Mod+X` Cut; `Mod+V` Paste; `Delete`/`Backspace` Clear these cells; `Alt+ArrowUp` Move up; `Alt+ArrowDown` Move down; `Mod+Alt+-` Delete ; `Mod+A` Select all: the words of the box, then everything; `Mod+Enter` Done; `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` Indent or bring out in a list; the next cell in a grid; `F2` Edit the cell, the caret at its end; `Shift+ArrowUp`/`Shift+ArrowDown`/`Shift+ArrowLeft`/`Shift+ArrowRight` Extend the selection; `Space` Tick or untick a task; `Escape` Step out: close, collapse, let go; `Escape` Put back what the cell held; `Enter`/`Shift+Enter`/`ArrowDown`/`ArrowUp`/`ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` The next or the one before.
- **Calculator**: `Enter` Done; `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` The next or the one before; `Escape` Clear the line; `Mod+A` Select all: the words of the box, then everything; `Enter` Done; `Escape` Step out: close, collapse, let go; `Alt+ArrowUp`/`Alt+ArrowDown` Move the selected items up or down; `Shift+ArrowUp`/`Shift+ArrowDown` Extend the selection; `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` The next or the one before; `Mod+D` Duplicate; `Mod+A` Select all: the words of the box, then everything; `Backspace` Delete.
- **Drawing Tool**: `V` Select; `R` Rectangle; `E` Ellipse; `D` Diamond; `L` Line; `A` Arrow; `T` Text; `K`/`Shift+K` Join two shapes; `P` Pen; `F` Freehand; `[` Rotate left; `]` Rotate right; `Enter` Edit the words; `Mod+D` Duplicate; `Mod+C` Copy; `Mod+X` Cut; `Mod+V` Paste; `Delete`/`Backspace` Delete; `Enter` Done; `Escape` Step out: close, collapse, let go; `Backspace` Delete; `Escape` Step out: close, collapse, let go; `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`/`ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`/`Enter` Join two shapes; `Mod+A` Select all: the words of the box, then everything; `Mod+Shift+L` Align: left; `Mod+Shift+E` Align: centre; `Mod+Shift+R` Align: right; `Alt+ArrowUp`/`Alt+ArrowDown` Move the selected items up or down; `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`/`ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`/`Shift+ArrowLeft`/`Shift+ArrowRight`/`Shift+ArrowUp`/`Shift+ArrowDown`/`Mod+ArrowLeft`/`Mod+ArrowRight`/`Mod+ArrowUp`/`Mod+ArrowDown` Nudge the shapes in hand; `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`/`ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` Tap or drag to paint; the arrow keys move, Enter paints.; `Enter`/`Space` Tap or drag to paint; the arrow keys move, Enter paints..
- **Diagram Maker**: `Alt+ArrowUp` Move up; `Alt+ArrowDown` Move down; `Tab` Indent; `Shift+Tab` Bring out; `Mod+D` Duplicate; `Mod+C` Copy; `Mod+X` Cut; `Mod+V` Paste; `Delete`/`Backspace` Delete; `Enter`/`Space` Edit; `Mod+Alt+ArrowLeft` Move left; `Mod+Alt+ArrowRight` Move right; `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`/`ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` The next or the one before; `ArrowDown`/`ArrowRight` The next or the one before; `Escape` Step out: close, collapse, let go; `Mod+Enter` Done.
- **Animator**: `Space` Play; `K` Add a key here; `Enter` Edit the words; `Mod+D` Duplicate; `Mod+C` Copy; `Mod+X` Cut; `Mod+V` Paste; `Delete`/`Backspace` Delete; `,`/`.` A frame back, a frame on; `Home`/`End` The first frame, the last; `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`/`ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`/`Shift+ArrowLeft`/`Shift+ArrowRight`/`Shift+ArrowUp`/`Shift+ArrowDown`/`Mod+ArrowLeft`/`Mod+ArrowRight`/`Mod+ArrowUp`/`Mod+ArrowDown` Nudge the shapes in hand; with none, step a frame; `Mod+A` Select all: the words of the box, then everything; `Escape` Step out: close, collapse, let go.
- **Calendar**: `Mod+Alt+ArrowLeft` A day earlier; `Mod+Alt+ArrowRight` A day later; `Alt+Enter` Dates; `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` Indent or bring out in a list; the next cell in a grid; `Alt+ArrowUp`/`Alt+ArrowDown` Move the selected items up or down; `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` The next or the one before; `Mod+D` Duplicate; `Mod+Enter` Tick or untick a task; `Mod+Alt+ArrowLeft` A day earlier; `Mod+Alt+ArrowRight` A day later; `Alt+Enter` Dates; `Enter` Event; `Escape` Step out: close, collapse, let go; `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`/`ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`/`Shift+ArrowLeft`/`Shift+ArrowRight`/`Shift+ArrowUp`/`Shift+ArrowDown`/`Home`/`End`/`PageUp`/`PageDown` The next or the one before; `Delete`/`Backspace` Delete; `Mod+D` Duplicate.
- **Trip Planner**: `Mod+Alt+Enter` Present; `Alt+ArrowUp`/`Alt+ArrowDown` Move the selected items up or down; `Mod+D` Duplicate; `ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown` The next or the one before; `ArrowRight`/`Space`/`PageDown`/`Enter` Presenting: the next stop; `ArrowLeft`/`PageUp`/`Backspace` Presenting: the stop before; `Home`/`End` The first, the last; `Escape` Stop presenting; `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight`/`ArrowUp`/`ArrowDown`/`Shift+ArrowLeft`/`Shift+ArrowRight`/`Shift+ArrowUp`/`Shift+ArrowDown` Nudge the shapes in hand; `Delete`/`Backspace` Delete; `Escape` Step out: close, collapse, let go.

## Choosing an app

- Numbers, a table, a chart, a model: `sheet`. A quick sum or a conversion: `calc`.
- Words to read or print: `write`. Notes in a tree: `outline`. Something to present: `deck`. A poster, a zine, badges: `deck` with a `format`.
- Ideas branching from one topic: `diagram` `mind`. People and reporting lines: `org`. A process with handoffs: `lanes`. Dates along a line: `timeline`. Overlaps: `venn`. Who sits where: `seating`. What talks to what: `net`.
- Days and times: `cal`; tasks over weeks: `cal` with `view: gantt`. Places in order: `trip`. Things to tick off: `- [ ]` tasks in `write` or `outline`.
- Anything else visual: `draw`; moving: `anim`.

## Good practice

- URL-encode `doc` and `title`; check that `#`, `&`, `%`, `+` and `=` in the content are encoded.
- Give the link as a Markdown link with a plain description: `[Sales by quarter (chart)](https://...)`.
- Say that the link is the document: editing it changes the link, and anyone with the link can read it.
